articles.title: Joe Milton Joins Cowboys Practice Squad After QB Goes Unclaimed on Waivers
articles.summary: Although the Dallas Cowboys waived quarterback Joe Milton, he is remaining with the organization after signing with the practice squad.
articles.body:
Although the Dallas Cowboys waived quarterback Joe Milton, he is remaining with the organization after signing with the practice squad.

Both COO/co-owner Stephen Jones and head coach Brian Schottenheimer had expressed significant interest in having the signal-caller back in the mix via the practice squad after his release earlier in the week.

Jones made his remarks on the DLLS Cowboys podcast, and Schottenheimer revealed his feelings to reporters during his Tuesday press conference.

The Cowboys were fortunate to get that chance to bring him back after Milton went unclaimed on waivers.

Milton initially made the 53-man roster after cuts were announced on Sunday. However, Dallas changed course after claiming running back Emari Demercado off waivers from the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday.

The Cowboys started with three quarterbacks on the 53-man roster in starter Dak Prescott, Milton and Sam Howell, although it was unclear who the Cowboys would choose to be Prescott's backup.

Schottenheimer had this to say on the matter Monday, per ESPN's Todd Archer , after the Demercado signing became official (and before Milton was let go).

"We're still piecing the puzzle together, and that's where this thing is very fluid," Schottenheimer said.

The Cowboys ultimately chose Howell as their QB2, making a switch from 2025, when Milton was Prescott's backup. Schottenheimer explained why.

"I think when we looked at the whole body of work, we just felt like Sam had done a little bit more in terms of executing the offense in certain areas," Schottenheimer told reporters on Tuesday, per DallasCowboys.com Staff Writer Tommy Yarrish .

"To have Joe Milton back would be incredible, we'll see what happens with the claims, and then see what he wants to do. We've shown that we know how to develop him. I think him being in this system for another year would be amazing, but I also know that he should have choices. And so, we'll see what happens, but in terms of wanting [Milton] back, absolutely."

Schottenheimer also said it was a "very, very hard decision" en route to choosing Howell, who signed a one-year deal with Dallas this offseason.

Milton did quite well this preseason, completing 29-of-43 passes (67.4 percent) for 378 yards and three touchdowns. Howell impressed as well, going 27-of-40 (67.5 percent) for 314 yards, three touchdowns and one interception.

Howell won the battle, but Milton could still be a part of the team's future.

Dallas opens the regular season on Sunday, Sept. 13 at the New York Giants.

articles.title: Lamar Jackson Contract Extension Talks Updated By Ravens GM Ahead of 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson's five-year, $260 million contract expires after the 2027 season, but general manager Eric DeCosta expressed optimism that the team can get an extension done with the two-time NFL MVP by March during a chat with reporters on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson's five-year, $260 million contract expires after the 2027 season, but general manager Eric DeCosta expressed optimism that the team can get an extension done with the two-time NFL MVP by March during a chat with reporters on Wednesday.

Jackson, who is entering his ninth season with the Ravens, is a four-time Pro Bowler and three-time First Team All-Pro who has led Baltimore to the playoffs in six of his campaigns.

Jackson's 8.3 adjusted passing yards per attempt and 102.2 quarterback rating stand first all-time in NFL history, per Pro Football Reference . He's also led the Ravens to a 76-31 record in his starts. Needless to say, it behooves the Ravens to keep the 29-year-old Jackson aboard long-term.

Last year was a tougher campaign for Jackson, who suffered multiple injuries, missed four games and saw his production dip after a 2024 season that ended with him finishing second in the NFL MVP race. Jackson told reporters in August that injuries in particular limited his mobility.

He goes into this season healthy, though, and that represents a chance Jackson can return to his usual form as a game-breaking dual threat.

If so, one can surmise his value would only go up. It's unclear what kind of contract Jackson, who is his own agent, would covet. At the top of the QB market , though, sits Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes and his $448 million deal ($64 million average per year).

Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson leads the NFL in total guarantees ($230 million) on his fully guaranteed five-year deal that ends after this season, though one can surmise that's something we may never see for a long time after the contract backfired on the team due to his poor performance.

Otherwise, Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen's $147 million guaranteed leads the way.

Negotiations between Jackson and the Ravens got ugly in March 2023, when Baltimore placed a non-exclusive franchise tag on the quarterback and Jackson requested a trade after saying "the team has not been interested in meeting my value." However, the two sides eventually came together for his current five-year deal, signed in April 2023.

The guess here, based on DeCosta's remarks, is that these negotiations could go smoother than the last time around. In the meantime, the Ravens are getting ready for Week 1 at the Indianapolis Colts on Sept. 13.

articles.title: Disgraced former Ravens kicker Justin Tucker reportedly works out for Jets
articles.summary: Tucker hasn't kicked in an NFL game since his release by the Ravens in 2025 after 16 women accused him of sexual misconduct.
articles.body:
Former Baltimore Ravens kicker Justin Tucker worked out for the New York Jets on Wednesday, according to multiple reports . Tucker was part of a group workout that also featured Michael Badgley and Josh Karty, NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports .

The Jets are in search of a kicker after Jason Sanders missed an extra point and a 54-yard field-goal attempt in Friday's preseason loss to the Giants, concluding a failed competition for the job from training camp. The Jets have since waived Sanders and claimed Blake Grupe off waivers. Sanders is back with the team on the practice squad.

Tucker was an eight-time Pro Bowler and five-time first-team All-Pro for the Baltimore Ravens in 13 seasons with the team. The Ravens released Tucker in 2025 after 16 women accused him of sexual misconduct that he allegedly engaged in repeatedly over the course of years during massage therapy sessions.

Tucker has denied the allegations and was not criminally charged.

Weeks after the Ravens cut Tucker, the NFL announced he was suspended for 10 games for violating the league's personal conduct policy. Tucker has not kicked in an NFL game since.

The Saints and Colts both reportedly worked Tucker out over the summer, but he did not make either roster. With New York's kicker position still unsettled, the Jets are giving Tucker a shot.

Tucker was one of the most accurate and reliable kickers in NFL history during his tenure with the Ravens. But his performance declined in his final season with the team prior to the news of the scandal and his release. He converted a career-low 73.3% of his field-goal attempts in 2024, well below his career conversion rate of 89.1%.

articles.title: Ashton Jeanty's Injury Status Revealed by Raiders HC Ahead of Week 1 vs. Dolphins
articles.summary: Despite an ankle injury scare during training camp, it seems as if Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty will be available for the team's Sept. 13 opener against the Miami Dolphins.
articles.body:
Despite an ankle injury scare during training camp, it seems as if Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty will be available for the team's Sept. 13 opener against the Miami Dolphins.

"Yes," Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak told reporters Wednesday when asked if he was optimistic Jeanty would play in that contest.

While initial reporting indicated there was significant concern among the running back's teammates when he suffered the injury and was helped off the field, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported last month he avoided a season-ending setback.

"It's nothing like that," Rapoport said. "My understanding... is that it's an ankle sprain believed to be more low than high, and not considered to be a major injury. But it is a real injury, and the reality is, there is a chance that Ashton Jeanty may not be on the field for Week 1. They are hopeful that he will be. There is a chance that he won't be."

Kubiak's comments suggest that Jeanty will be available against the Dolphins, although ESPN's Ryan McFadden reported he didn't practice Wednesday.

Jeanty surely wants to play against a Dolphins team that may be among the Raiders' more favorable opponents of the season.

That would give him an early opportunity to build on his solid but unspectacular play from his rookie season in 2025 when he tallied 975 yards and five touchdowns on the ground behind just 3.7 yards per carry.

Las Vegas made him a franchise building block when it selected him with the No. 6 overall pick of the 2025 NFL draft, and he didn't quite live up to elevated expectations in his first year in the league.

But Jeanty now has a season of experience under his belt and will look to take a second-year leap, assuming he is healthy enough to be on the field when the regular season starts.

articles.body: The San Francisco 49ers are on their way to Australia to participate in the first-ever NFL game on the continent against their NFC West foe, the Los Angeles Rams, to kick off the 2026 season. And two specific passengers have fans hopeful heading into next week’s matchup down under. Tight end George Kittle and defensive end Nick Bosa, two very important pieces of Kyle Shanahan’s roster, made the trip with the rest of the team, according to multiple reports. Kittle suffered a torn Achilles in the Wild Card Round against the Philadelphia Eagles on Jan. 11, while Bosa tore his ACL in Week 3 last season. articles.title: Travis Kelce health scare sparks Chiefs concern days before 2026 season opener
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce’s latest absence has put Kansas City Chiefs fans on alert just days before the team opens its 2026 campaign. The veteran tight end missed.
articles.body: Travis Kelce’s latest absence has put Kansas City Chiefs fans on alert just days before the team opens its 2026 campaign. The veteran tight end missed Kansas City’s annual kickoff luncheon on September 1 after reportedly feeling “under the weather.” While there is no indication of a serious health issue, the timing has naturally drawn attention as Kelce prepares for another demanding NFL season.Travis Kelce misses Chiefs kickoff luncheon amid health concernsThe update came through Kansas City Star reporter Pete Sweeney, who cited longtime Chiefs radio voice Mitch Holthus when reporting Kelce’s absence.“Travis Kelce is not at the Chiefs' annual kickoff luncheon. Under the weather, per Mitch Holthus,” Sweeney reported.That remains the clearest information available about Kelce’s condition. Neither the Chiefs nor the player has indicated that the illness is serious, and there has been no confirmation that it will prevent him from taking the field when Kansas City begins its season.Still, missing a major team event so close to opening day was enough to raise eyebrows.Kelce has plenty of motivation entering his 14th NFL season. The 36-year-old tight end chose to continue his career after considering retirement, and his comments during the offseason suggested that he still believes he has more to accomplish.“I've had a lot of success in the NFL, but I'm still reaching for that perfection,” Kelce told Vogue. “I still haven't played the perfect game.”His ambition has not faded with age. If anything, Kelce appears determined to make another serious run at success alongside quarterback Patrick Mahomes.“Year 14, baby, I'm fired up. Every year there's a chance to do something special, but especially coming into this year, getting Pat [Mahomes] back and wiping the slate clean.”Travis Kelce enters 2026 chasing another NFL milestoneKelce’s health update is particularly significant because he remains an important part of Kansas City’s offensive plans. Last season, he finished with 76 receptions for 851 yards. That followed a career-low 823 receiving yards in 2024, leading to questions about how much longer he can maintain his elite production.Chiefs coach Andy Reid, however, has continued to praise Kelce’s work ethic and conditioning.“You have examples like Kelce - he's the oldest guy on the team and came out every day and worked to where you had to yank him out of there to give him a breather,” Reid said.There is also history within reach.Kelce currently has 13,002 career receiving yards. He needs 45 more to move past Jason Witten and claim second place among tight ends on the NFL’s all-time receiving yardage list.For now, Kansas City has little reason to panic. Kelce was simply reported to be under the weather, with no further details released. articles.title: Ravens GM says team is still waiting on NFL investigation of Rashod Bateman's arrest
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens general manager Eric DeCosta says the team is still waiting on the NFL's investigation into receiver Rashod Bateman's arrest earlier this of...
articles.body:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. (AP) — Baltimore Ravens general manager Eric DeCosta says the team is still waiting on the NFL's investigation into receiver Rashod Bateman's arrest earlier this offseason.

"In these matters we just really kind of sit back and wait for the league and for the authorities to kind of tell us what's going on," DeCosta said. "Have no indication how long that's going to take."

Bateman was taken into custody in June in Georgia on suspicion of family violence battery and reckless conduct, both misdemeanors, and criminal damage to property, a felony.

"It's obviously something that we're very disappointed about, that we have to deal with these kind of things right now," DeCosta said. "We knew about it right away, we contacted the league right away. Spoke to the league, the league has been doing an investigation."

DeCosta spoke with reporters Wednesday, a normal occurrence shortly before the start of the season. In addition to Bateman's legal issues, he also addressed the team's kicking situation. Baltimore added Jake Moody to the practice squad this week, in effect putting starter Tyler Loop on notice after a shaky preseason.

Loop missed three of his seven field goal attempts in this year's exhibition games.

"We got to make kicks," DeCosta said. "Fresh set of legs to look at, evaluate, compare, see how it all works out. In the end, it's a performance business."

DeCosta also said he remains optimistic about working out a new contract with star quarterback Lamar Jackson. That did not happen this offseason, and the team ended up having to restructure his existing deal, which has two seasons remaining.

The biggest cause for optimism when Baltimore released its 53-man roster last weekend was the fact that defensive lineman Nnamdi Madubuike was not on injured reserve, which suggests he's expected back at some point in the first four weeks.

Madubuike missed most of last season with a neck injury.

"I'm as encouraged now as I've ever been about Nnamdi," DeCosta said. "Getting him back has been incredible."

articles.title: NFL expert urges 49ers to trade for Maxx Crosby
articles.summary: The 49ers may need to make a big trade to remain competitive in the tough NFC West.
articles.body:
The NFC West is a gauntlet heading into the 2026 NFL season, and the San Francisco 49ers may be falling behind. The Los Angeles Rams beefed up their defense with the additions of Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie before the return of Aaron Donald, and the defending division and Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks still look dominant.

Therefore, NFL Network analyst Brian Baldinger believes the 49ers must make a swing of their own and trade for Las Vegas Raiders star edge rusher Maxx Crosby. Speaking on 95.7 The Game , Baldinger framed the trade as a necessity given what the Rams have already done on the defensive line.

"You're in an arms race with the Rams right now," Baldinger said. "This is like a military arms race trying to keep up. I don't know that Maxx Crosby is available or could be had, I have no idea. All I know is I was at the Sack Summit in Las Vegas a month ago, and nobody could beat him off the line of scrimmage. Everybody challenged him — Jared Verse, pick a guy that was out there — nobody could beat him off the ball. Nobody. He won, and they had an open competition, Maxx — I got it on video — he beat everybody off the ball."

Baldinger also dismissed concerns about the knee issue that scuttled a trade to the Baltimore Ravens back in the spring, drawing on his own playing career for context.

"I know Baltimore basically said that his knee is shot," Baldinger said. "I don't see it. I failed a physical coming in after my sixth year, failed a physical, and played six more years. They said my knee was shot. Everybody evaluates these things differently. But I feel like if you had a chance to get Maxx Crosby, he becomes your best defensive player immediately. It's infectious, the way that he plays the game, the way that he practices. Shanahan's not going to beat him in the building. On any given day, he'll beat everybody in the building. He's got the Michael Jordan mentality."

What would it cost to acquire Crosby? The Ravens traded two first-round picks, but that package seems too pricey now given what unfolded with the deal earlier this year. Bleacher Report's Alex Kay proposed a deal built around a 2027 first-rounder, a 2027 second-rounder and a 2028 third-rounder to pry Crosby loose in the wake of the Rams' Myles Garrett trade.

However, Sports Illustrated 's Albert Breer urged caution with any deal, writing that he liked the idea "in principle" but preferred San Francisco wait and see how its aging core performed before selling off draft capital. Crosby himself carries a three-year, $106.5 million extension with $91.5 million guaranteed, signed after the Baltimore deal collapsed.

The 49ers need edge rushing help, though. Nick Bosa is working back from his ACL injury and Mykell Williams is already on the physically unable to perform list and won't play for at least the first four weeks of the season. That leaves a hobbled Bosa, 2026 rookie Romello Height, Sam Okuayinonu and Keion White as the only viable pass rushers on the edge at the moment for San Francisco.

Crosby would be expensive and risky, but likely worth it to remain competitive in the division.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers Reacts to Steelers Keeping 4 QBs in Rare Roster Move for 1st Time in Veteran's Career
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers reacted to the Pittsburgh Steelers keeping four quarterbacks on the team's 53-man roster heading into the 2026 season.
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers reacted to the Pittsburgh Steelers keeping four quarterbacks on the team's 53-man roster heading into the 2026 season.

"I was thinking it was a possibility, but I don't think I've been on a roster with four quarterbacks," Rodgers said Wednesday, per ESPN's Brooke Pryor .

"Obviously when you do that, you're taking away a spot from another place in the team," he added. "But at the same time, if the best 53 are going to make it -- and not saying they did -- I think those four are part of the best 53."

Rodgers will be on an active roster that contains four signal-callers for the first time in his career. Pittsburgh's quarterback room includes Mason Rudolph, Drew Allar and Will Howard.

Rudolph has spent five seasons with the Steelers while primarily operating in a reserve role. Pittsburgh selected Howard with a sixth-round pick in the 2025 NFL draft before adding Allar with a third-round pick in the 2026 draft.

"I'm happy for all those guys," Rodgers said, per Pryor. "Obviously looking to the future, those other three guys are going to have a chance when I'm done. And with the growth you saw with Will and obviously with Drew being drafted so far, but also playing well in camp, I'm not surprised at all and I'm excited about those guys' future."

The 42-year-old is the unquestioned starter in Pittsburgh and has appeared in 33 of a possible 34 regular-season games over the past two years, but it's worth noting that he previously suffered a torn Achilles in Week 1 of his 2023 campaign.

If Rodgers misses time in 2026, Rudolph is the only backup quarterback with regular-season experience on his résumé. Still, the Steelers weren't interested in parting ways with Howard or Allar after recently drafting them.

Pittsburgh will open its 2026 season against the Atlanta Falcons on Sept. 13.

articles.title: 'I mean, clearly,' Jalen Hurts tells GQ when asked if he and A.J. Brown grew apart in Philadelphia
articles.summary: Jalen Hurts confirmed to GQ that he and A.J. Brown "clearly" grew apart before the wide receiver was traded to the New England Patriots in June.
articles.body: After an uneven 2025 season for Jalen Hurts, A.J. Brown and the Eagles’ offense as a whole, Philadelphia traded Brown to the Patriots for a pair of future draft picks. The blockbuster move came amid signs that Hurts’ once-close friendship between the franchise quarterback and star receiver had deteriorated. While more than two months have passed since Brown's move to New England, questions about his relationship with Hurts have lingered. During the Patriots’ recent joint practices with the Eagles, Brown offered a one-word response when asked whether he had spoken with Hurts since the trade. "No," Brown told reporters. While Hurts has largely avoided discussing the state of his relationship with Brown, he took a different approach this week during a sit-down interview with GQ. "There's no surprise that it was talked about," Hurts told the magazine when asked whether he and Brown had remained close, acknowledging the shift in the relationship. Hurts, the MVP of Super Bowl LIX, then effectively confirmed Brown's comments from last month, saying, "I mean, clearly," Hurts noted. In June, Brown said no single incident had sparked the rift between the two former Eagles teammates. "Nothing happened, people just grow apart. Nothing happened between me and him, or ‌our families, ⁠wives, anything. Nothing like that ever happened," Brown said at the time during an appearance on the "7PM in Brooklyn with Carmelo Anthony" podcast. AJ BROWN SAYS THERE'S BEEN SILENCE BETWEEN HIM AND EX-TEAMMATE JALEN HURTS SINCE HIS MOVE TO NEW ENGLAND "Life happens, and you just look up sometimes and you just, you find yourself drifting away, and that's fine. The Eagles won the franchise’s second Vince Lombardi Trophy the following season, despite some drama involving Brown. Brown then told the Eagles' front office he wanted a change of scenery, general manager Howie Roseman said at the time. Sources told ESPN that part of Brown's frustration centered on Hurts and a belief that he was not being targeted enough when he faced zone coverage. Brown also made several social media comments and comments during media sessions during the 2025 season that appeared to reflect frustration with his role in the offense. While Brown expressed gratitude for his time in the City of Brotherly Love, he said he's turned his attention to a new season with a new team. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "It's love. I won a Super Bowl ring with them. It will always be love no matter how anyone feels. I love Philly and I will always love Philly, but I'm here now," said Brown. "That's where my feet are and that's what I'm focused on." Long before they became Eagles teammates, Hurts hosted Brown on a recruiting visit to Alabama. Their friendship deepened through offseason workouts, and Hurts eventually became godfather to Brown’s daughter, Jersee. articles.title: Philadelphia man charged for attempted break-in at Eagles star Saquon Barkley's home in July
articles.summary: While people were home at the time of the attempted break-in, Saquon Barkley said that nobody was hurt during the incident.
articles.body:
A Philadelphia man has been arrested and charged with multiple felonies after an attempted break-in at the home of Eagles star Saquon Barkley earlier this summer.

Jabir Parker, 24, was arrested Tuesday and is facing charges related to two break-ins and the attempted break-in of a third home in the Philadelphia area this summer, according to NBC10 .

The first two break-ins, per the report, were successful. Parker allegedly broke into a home on June 22 and stole roughly $107,000 worth of jewelry. A few weeks later, Parker allegedly stole more than $687,000 worth of jewelry from a second home.

The third attempt, on July 18, was the one at Barkley's home. While officials did not name the owners of the home involved, NBC10 reported that it is owned by Barkley and his family.

"In the third burglary, the … homeowners were awakened by suspicious sounds before finding an unknown male inside the home and calling 911," the district attorney said.

Barkley told NBC10 that nobody inside the home was hurt. He has since taken up extra security.

Parker is facing multiple felonies, including burglary and conspiracy to burglary. He is still in custody as of Wednesday afternoon, and is due in court on Sept. 10.

Dallas Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb had more than $300,000 worth of luxury bags stolen from his Texas home during training camp, according to police. Both Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders and Tennessee titans lineman Jeffery Simmons had their homes broken into during the 2025 season, and seven individuals were charged in February for allegedly burglarizing the homes of Chiefs stars Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce, among others.

Barkley ran for 1,140 yards and had nine total touchdowns last season, his second with the Eagles after helping them to their Super Bowl win the year before. The Eagles will open the season against the Washington Commanders on Sept. 13.

articles.title: 49ers Down Under: ABC7 Eyewitness News heads to Melbourne for Niner's season opener against Rams
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers are heading Down Under to open their NFL season against the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne, and ABC7 Eyewitness News will have complet...
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers are heading Down Under to open their NFL season against the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne, and ABC7 Eyewitness News will have complete coverage from Australia and the Bay Area.

ABC7's J.R. Stone will have live reports from Melbourne in the lead-up to the season opener and the latest on how 49ers fans are enjoying everything Australia has to offer.

The Niners will leave Wednesday night from California, arrive in Melbourne Friday morning, and then take time to adjust to the new time zone. They will hold a light practice on Saturday, take Sunday off and then have a normal stretch of three practices on Monday through Wednesday before playing the opener on Friday morning.

They will leave right after the game and are expected to land back in the Bay Area on Friday afternoon. They then will be able to take the weekend off before preparing for the Week 2 game against Miami on Sept. 20.

"It's a big adjustment on the body," coach Kyle Shanahan said. "So, the recommendation for everybody has been to tell us when to go, and it's made a lot of sense. I know how our players feel also. I was a little bit on the fence. Science wasn't and what I was reported on and our players weren't at all. So that helped me get off the fence."

The Rams consulted with their own scientists and came up with the opposite approach. They will do most of their practice at home and aren't expected to arrive in Australia until about 24 hours before the game, hoping the short stay leads to no jet lag.

The better option might not be known until after the game.

The approach by the Niners has made the past few days a whirlwind. The players got the weekend off after playing the final exhibition game on Thursday night in Las Vegas and resumed practice on Monday - the day after the roster was reduced to 53 players.

The front office had to make those cuts, put together a practice squad and figure out which players would be healthy for Week 1 to make sure they had the correct roster in place before departing.

"There's a lot behind the scenes," general manager John Lynch said. "Our logistics folks, our folks that work in the cafe, have just gone to tremendous lengths, our health and performance team, to make sure that we're giving our players the best opportunity to feel right when they play down there in Australia. Everything from getting visas, which much more complicated than I ever knew, and they've been outstanding. ... Hats off to those guys for pulling off a monumental task, and it's not done yet."

Lynch said he had to make sure all the practice squad players he wanted to sign had passports with one needing his parents to send it overnight. It was an even bigger scramble for offensive lineman Jarrett Patterson, who was acquired in a trade from Houston on Sunday.

"They were like, hey, do you have a passport? We're leaving for Australia in three days," he said. "I was like, 'Whoa!' It's obviously a quick turnaround getting here a couple hours after I found out and now getting ready for Australia."

But in all, the players are welcoming the challenge and opportunity. Cornerback Deommodore Lenoir said he'd travel 30 hours if needed to play in an NFL game and rookie De'Zhaun Stribling has a must-see item on his to-do list before making his debut.

"I kind of want to see a kangaroo, just because," he said. "To see how big they are."

The opener against the Rams will have an additional challenge after the Rams brought Aaron Donald out of retirement to join Myles Garrett on one of the fiercest defensive lines in the game.

Donald is a three-time AP Defensive Player of the Year but was out of football the past two seasons. His 12 1/2 career sacks against the 49ers in the regular season and playoffs are tied with Kevin Greene for the most ever.

"They got better, certainly, with him deciding to come out of retirement," Lynch said. "Now, there's time away. But I know that guy trains like a madman. I ran into him in a hotel somewhere a while back and we had some fun chatter back and forth. Never thought he'd do it. But he's doing it and so we better get ready for it."

If you are heading to Melbourne to watch the 49ers, share your experience with ABC7 Eyewitness News!

The Associated Press contributed to this article.

articles.title: NFL QB pressure index 2026: Joe Burrow, Justin Herbert among QBs with most to prove
articles.summary: Being an NFL quarterback means constant pressure to perform -- but these 9 passers have a bit more riding on the 2026 season.
articles.body:
Being an NFL quarterback means constant pressure to succeed.

Every game, from Week 1 onward, will be used as data by fans to measure how good a passer and their team is. With a few bad outings, injury issues, or a failure to live up to high expectations, in the blink of an eye, a starter may become a backup — there are only 32 QB1 spots to go around.

A case can be made that every NFL quarterback has some kind of pressure to succeed in the 2026 season. Even Sam Darnold, fresh off a Super Bowl victory, may be out to prove his 2025 was no fluke. But some quarterbacks have more riding on the upcoming season than others.

Here's a ranking of the nine quarterbacks facing the most pressure to succeed in 2026.

Tina MacIntyre-Yee/Democrat and Chronicle / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images

Josh Allen turned 30 years old in May. He's tracking to be one of the greatest quarterbacks of all-time, one of the biggest stars of his era and should have plenty more elite years left in the tank. However, with every year he doesn't reach a Super Bowl, the Bills have more questions to answer — and it already reached a tipping point this offseason.

Sean McDermott, the only coach Allen had ever played for in Buffalo, was fired after yet another heartbreaking playoff loss, the seventh consecutive season in which the Bills made the playoffs with at least 10 wins but failed to reach the Super Bowl. And this time, Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs weren't even to blame.

Even with Kansas City taking a step back in 2025, Buffalo couldn't emerge from the AFC. Yet, at this point, there's still almost an expectation that come every January, the Bills will be in the playoffs thanks to Allen's talents.

Here's their regular season record and playoff result in every season since Allen took over in 2018:

2019: 10-6 (lost to Texans in wild card)

2020: 13-3 (lost to Chiefs in AFC Championship)

2021: 11-6 (lost to Chiefs in divisional round)

2022: 13-3 (lost to Bengals in divisional round)

2023: 11-6 (lost to Chiefs in divisional round)

2024: 13-4 (lost to Chiefs in AFC Championship)

2025: 12-5 (lost to Broncos in divisional round)

The Bills have lived and died by Allen's performances for years, whether that's fair or not. It's the way their offense is designed and how they have won so many games. With Joe Brady taking over as head coach, there may not be anybody else to blame if the Bills can't make a Super Bowl push in 2026.

There's no chance the Bills move on from Allen next offseason, even in a worst-case scenario, but he's only going to be a Super Bowl-level quarterback for so long. With every missed opportunity in Buffalo, Allen's career trajectory looks more like Dan Marino.

Put Joe Burrow in the same category as Allen. They're both veteran star quarterbacks who have consistently come up short of a ring, primarily because of Mahomes' Chiefs, who also failed to step up in the AFC last year despite Kansas City's struggles. There are two key differences with Burrow: he has been to a Super Bowl, and he's set to hit free agency a year before Allen, in 2030.

That year of difference in contract length — especially with Cincinnati missing the playoffs in three straight years — means the results of 2026 could wind up dictating Burrow's long-term future with the team. Partly due to his injury issues, the Bengals haven't been an AFC contender since their 2022 loss to the Chiefs in the AFC Championship Game.

Here's how the Bengals have performed since Burrow took over as quarterback in 2020:

2022: 12-4 (lost to Chiefs in AFC Championship Game)

For a quarterback of Burrow's caliber, four missed playoffs in six years won't cut it. With every disappointment in Cincinnati, pressure mounts on them to succeed before there's a threat of Burrow departing while still in his prime.

It's not yet a realistic threat to consider the Bengals needing to move on from Burrow. But if you picture the end of the 2026 season, if the team misses the playoffs again, that may become a question it has to answer sooner than expected. That also puts pressure on Burrow to not just stay healthy, but prove he's still capable of the heights he's reached in 2021 and 2022.

Through three NFL seasons, C.J. Stroud's best was his first, when he threw for over 4,000 yards and 23 touchdowns as he became a star for the Texans . Since then, he simply has not been great enough for Houston's offense to be a Super Bowl threat.

By now, it's clear that the Texans have the defensive talent to contend for a title; that side of the ball was the backbone of their 12-win season in 2025. If Stroud can distribute the ball at the elite rate he was in 2023, there's a chance that the Texans make national noise.

The Texans are a good team with Stroud leading the way. That much is clear. The question is whether they can be a great team, something that can only happen with the best version of their quarterback.

There's also an intriguing contract angle to Stroud's 2026 season — he has yet to come to terms on a rookie extension with Houston, carrying a club option for 2027 before 2028 free agency. With a bad season for the Texans, perhaps they're unwilling to sign Stroud to a contract that compares to his peers.

If Stroud can't uplift Houston's offense this season, he's another big name whose future could be up in the air.

There may be no more obvious quarterback facing pressure in their career this NFL season than Tua Tagovailoa. The Dolphins accepted a record-setting $99.2 million total dead cap just to release him this offseason, which isn't exactly a vote of confidence in his abilities. Add in his concussion/injury history and a preseason competition with Michael Penix Jr., and Tagovailoa has had a bit of a fall from grace.

Even with Penix not playing throughout training camp, Atlanta has been unwilling to name Tagovailoa as its starter. Just two seasons ago, he led the NFL in passing yards. But already, with one more rough stretch, Tagovailoa could be staring down becoming a rest-of-career backup.

In the best-case scenario, Tagovailoa can maximize the Falcons ' offensive weapons and Kevin Stefanski's play calling, holding onto the starting quarterback job and setting himself for a longer-term deal next offseason. Anything other than that, though, will make his NFL future far murkier.

Any quarterback who needs a competition to win the starting job faces pressure. But Tagovailoa's injury history and historic release from the Dolphins make him even more of a make-or-break candidate for 2026.

To this point, the Buccaneers have been unable to come to an extension agreement with Baker Mayfield, who has led the team since 2023. His time in Tampa Bay has included two playoff trips but just one 10-plus-win season, and while Mayfield has put up strong numbers, the Buccaneers have been unable to become a true NFC threat.

Tampa Bay seems to have a high floor every year, with the offensive talent to compete with virtually any opponent. But the team needs Mayfield at his best to contend for the NFC South title, and as he enters Year 9 of his up-and-down career, the quarterback hasn't proven he can go on a deep playoff run.

Mayfield's contract situation is perhaps the most intriguing of any NFL starting quarterback. If he can't lead the Buccaneers to the playoffs this fall, he may be on a new team in 2027.

Another AFC quarterback who hasn't been able to overcome Mahomes' shadow? Justin Herbert. The Chargers QB has regularly made his club good — like Stroud or Mayfield with their teams — but it's still unclear if he can lead a team to the promised land.

Herbert typically doesn't receive much blame for the Chargers' inability to break through, because for the most part, he's been consistently great despite issues surrounding him, whether on the offensive line or defensively. But at some point, the NFL is always about quarterback play.

Regardless of an injury to center Tyler Biadasz, there's a clear path for the Chargers to be the AFC West's best team in 2026. Unlike counterparts like Allen or Burrow, however, Herbert hasn't been able to lead L.A. even past the wild-card round. If that happens again, it could lead to more significant changes for the franchise, even if Herbert is around for the long-term.

The final AFC quarterback on this list, Lamar Jackson, is one who has individually dominated every NFL season, but also hasn't put it all together for a Super Bowl run.

There are no longer any questions about Jackson's capabilities as a passer, and we've known for years he can run with the best offensive weapons in the NFL. But with one conference championship appearance to Jackson's name and a missed playoff trip in 2025, John Harbaugh was let go, shifting some of the focus to the Ravens ' star quarterback to prove that was the right decision.

The reason Jackson ranks lower than Allen or Burrow here, however, is partially due to the fact that Jackson can't be fully blamed for Baltimore's 2025 struggles, throwing for 21 touchdowns and seven interceptions. There's a clear overall trend of his individual excellence every year despite the team coming up short.

The pressure in Baltimore for 2026 is more on Jessie Minter and the Ravens' defense than Jackson and the offense. But as noted with other quarterbacks, at the end of the day, the players at that position are expected to lead their team regardless of circumstances. Jackson still hasn't reached the biggest stage in football despite his electric play.

Another Eagles season, another new playcaller for Jalen Hurts. With a Super Bowl ring to his name, Hurts deserves more leeway than most NFL quarterbacks, but with Philadelphia's offense struggling in 2025, he needs to prove that was due to the playcalling and not his limitations on the field.

Everywhere Hurts has gone, he's been a winner. He hasn't missed the playoffs yet as an NFL starter. But merely making the dance is no longer the expectation for Hurts — once he proved he could lead Philadelphia to the Super Bowl, Eagles fans' appetites changed. Anything but NFC East crowns and deep playoff runs is considered a disappointment, which is a high, but fair bar to set.

Hurts' 2025 numbers (11-5 record, 25 touchdowns, six interceptions) don't indicate he needs much of a bounce-back season, but there needs to be offensive improvement in Philadelphia with Sean Marrion at offensive coordinator and A.J. Brown gone. If Hurts can't answer the doubters this time, with just two years remaining on his deal after 2026, his future in the City of Brotherly Love could look a bit different.

John Jones - IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

Rounding out the list is a quarterback in a very similar situation to Tagovailoa, but with a better track record and system around him: Kyler Murray. The Cardinals made the expensive decision to let him go this offseason, and while Murray has flashed plenty of elite arm talent and dual-threat capabilities, it hasn't led to any kind of team success in the NFL.

Murray, hypothetically, now has everything he needs to succeed: an offensive-minded head coach, some elite weapons around him, a QB1 job and a winning culture in Minnesota. It's clear that he has the talent to succeed, but his motivation has been called into question. In a contract year, those are questions that need to be answered.

Murray is playing on a one-year deal with the Vikings, making this a make-or-break year for him. His talent would still likely give him more future opportunities, but no team is going to be willing to sign him to a significant contract in free agency next spring if he can't keep Minnesota competitive.

articles.title: Latest Fantasy Football Mock Draft After the 2026 Preseason
articles.summary: Summer is winding down—and so is fantasy draft season. Labor Day marks the unofficial end of the former, while the first game of the 2026 NFL season on Wednesday, Sept. 9, effectively closes the latter.
articles.body:
Summer is winding down—and so is fantasy draft season. Labor Day marks the unofficial end of the former, while the first game of the 2026 NFL season on Wednesday, Sept. 9, effectively closes the latter.

Most fantasy managers have already drafted their teams for the coming season, but one final draft weekend remains for those still assembling their first—or perhaps their 21st—roster.

As they have all summer, tools such as rankings and ADP information remain valuable for managers preparing for their drafts. Recent draft trends can be useful, too, especially after all the changes of the past few weeks.

The Bleacher Report Mock That Isn't Charity Challenge is a live fantasy league rather than a conventional mock draft. Participants—including B/R analysts Kris Knox and Maurice Moton , experienced fantasy players and a mystery novelist—will manage their teams throughout the season.

The live-league format helps ensure participants take the draft seriously, making the results more useful to fantasy managers.

The mini-run at wide receiver offered up some values at running back in the back half of Round 1—and Cook was the best of the lot. He led the NFL last year with 1,621 rushing yards, and he has scored at least a dozen rushing touchdowns in each of the past two seasons.

McCaffrey was fantasy's No. 1 back last year, and he's capable of not only finishing first at the position but blowing the competition away. He's also a 30-year-old back coming off a historic season who led the league with 413 touches last year. The seasons following his first two 2,000-yard seasons from scrimmage were ugly: He missed 13 games in each.

Getting Jeanty at the back of Round 1 could be a bargain or a waste—it all depends on his ankle injury and whether that lingers into the season. He was regularly falling into Round 2 after getting hurt, but this selection could signal a rebound heading into the final draft weekend of 2026.

Williams has taken something of a tumble down draft boards this summer—ostensibly because of Blake Corum's increasing workload over the second half of last season. But Williams was more effective on a per-touch basis last year than in 2024, and he has posted top-10 fantasy numbers among running backs three years running.

The Seahawks used their first pick in April's draft on Price, but even with Zach Charbonnet on injured reserve to start the season, there has been no indication that Price will be a bell-cow back. His Average Draft Position is in Round 5 this summer.

Biggest Surprise: Justin Jefferson at 2.02

Yes, Jefferson had a down 2025 season—at least by his stratospheric standards. But it's still a little weird to see him available in Round 2. If you believe that Kyler Murray's arrival in the Twin Cities will spur an offensive rebound in 2026, then Jefferson should be one of the bigger beneficiaries—and a value pick at No. 14 overall.

With the managers in this draft hitting the running back position hard early, there were some values to be had at wide receiver. Collins was the best of those values in Round 3. He has topped 1,000 receiving yards each of the past three seasons and is widely considered a top-10 fantasy option.

McConkey is coming off a disappointing second season—after 1,149 receiving yards as a rookie he failed to hit 800 yards in Year 2. He's a talented wideout who should see a bump in targets this year, but seeing McConkey come off the board ahead of Collins, Malik Nabers and Rashee Rice was eyebrow-raising.

Biggest Surprise: Jeremiyah Love at 3.06

Like Ashton Jeanty, Love heads into the 2026 season with a bad ankle after getting hurt in his preseason debut. Like Jeanty, that injury has caused Love's asking price to ping-pong all over the place. With that said, getting the third overall pick from April's draft in the middle of Round 3 makes the risk a bit more palatable.

The fantasy manager who earned the first pick in the draft played the first four rounds exceedingly well. Joe Mixon was a top-10 back in PPR points per game two years ago as the featured back in Houston, and Montgomery was a top-five fantasy option the only time in his career he logged 300 touches in a season.

Compared to ADP, getting Allen in the middle of Round 4 is good value—he typically comes off the board more than 15 picks earlier. However, selecting the first quarterback does not always pay off: The edge Allen provided at the position last season was only about one fantasy point per game.

Biggest Surprise: Jameson Williams at 4.09

Williams has shown high-end fantasy upside—the young speedster topped 1,100 receiving yards last year and finished as the WR12 in PPR points . But while he has a sky-high fantasy ceiling he can also be high-variance—it was a little surprising to see him go ahead of a higher-floor option such as Tetairoa McMillan.

In terms of average draft position, Higgins is coming off the board with the last selection in Round 3 as the 17th wide receiver. That price (in the opinion of this analyst) is a tad steep. However, getting Higgins over a round after that as the 23rd receiver taken is a solid value pick.

You can argue that Dobbins is going later than he should on average—he'll be the lead back for the Broncos so long as he can stay healthy. But the caveat "so long as he can stay healthy" is a major one, and in this particular draft Dobbins went at No. 53 overall—over three rounds earlier than his ADP of 94.

Biggest Surprise: Running Back Panic Attack

The managers in this draft were not shy about selecting running backs, as they came off the board at an unusually rapid rate in Round 5. Half the round's picks were running backs, including both members of the Denver and Pittsburgh backfield committees. That early run pushed the draft into the "RB Dead Zone" sooner than usual.

In terms of ADP, this is right around where Stevenson is usually going. But this is less about where Stevenson was drafted than who he was drafted after—getting New England's lead running back after backs like Rico Dowdle of the Steelers and Aaron Jones of the Vikings was a bargain.

Lloyd's ADP has risen sharply with Josh Jacobs unavailable, but he is also a third-year pro who has played in just one game over the past two seasons and has only six career carries for 15 yards.

Biggest Surprise: Matthew Stafford at 6.08

Last year, Stafford threw for 4,707 yards and 46 touchdown passes, finishing second among quarterbacks in fantasy points. He plays for a Rams team loaded with offensive weapons. Still, seeing the 2025 NFL MVP selected as the fifth quarterback off the board was jarring given his QB13 ADP and typical 10th-round price tag.

There appears to have been some skepticism among these drafters as to whether it will be Odunze or Luther Burden III who emerges as the No. 1 wide receiver for the Bears this year. But it's hard to argue the value of getting Odunze in the middle of Round 7—that's about a round and a half after he's being selected on average.

Were Kittle 100 percent healthy, this wouldn't be a bad pick at all—Kittle is routinely a top-five fantasy option in terms of fantasy points per game. But Kittle is also a 32-year-old tight end who missed a chunk of last season—and then tore his Achilles in the playoffs. He's a risky choice as a top-five tight end.

In many fantasy drafts this summer, the tight ends in the TE5 to TE10 range have kind of trickled off the board—the gap in ADP between the two is about three rounds. But that wasn't the case in this draft. Five tight ends came off the board in Round 7, tying wide receivers for the most players selected at any position.

No running backs were drafted in the seventh round.

Even at his WR33 ADP, Metcalf has a case as a value after finishing as a low-end WR2 in PPR points per game last season. He was an even better value in this draft, coming off the board more than a round later than his average cost as the 37th wide receiver selected.

Goff has been a valuable fantasy asset in recent years, logging three straight top-seven finishes among quarterbacks and finishing second in the league in passing yards last season. However, he is typically available much later than this: He is the 16th quarterback selected on average, with an ADP near the end of Round 10.

Biggest Surprise: Jordan Mason after Aaron Jones Sr.

As mentioned, this draft was unusually aggressive where the running back position is concerned—by round's end almost 40 were off the board and the cupboard was pretty bare. Jordan Mason of the Vikings was the first back taken in the round, but it was rather surprising to see him get taken after batterymate Aaron Jones given their respective average asking price in drafts.

Sutton was a strong value at this spot, even after Parker Washington came off the board earlier in the round. Even if Jaylen Waddle becomes Denver's top target this season, Sutton topped 1,000 receiving yards and finished among the top 25 fantasy wide receivers last year. At WR44, he was a steal.

This pick would look better if the manager who made it also had Jeremiyah Love rostered—Allgeier is one of the more valuable "handcuff" backs in 2026. But they do not, and there were a couple of backs taken after Allgeier who have a clearer path to carries than Allgeier does in the desert.

At least in this league, the managers appear unenthused about Hurts' fantasy prospects in 2026. Sure, A.J. Brown is gone, but the cupboard is hardly bare in Philadelphia. Hurts also offers significant rushing upside and has posted two top-five finishes over the past four seasons.

Johnston can admittedly be a maddening fantasy option—he'll post a huge game one week and then vanish for three more. But we're still talking about a player who scored eight touchdowns and finished inside fantasy WR3 territory last year. With Keenan Allen gone, Johnston should also see a target bump in 2026.

To be clear, there aren't really any "worst" picks in the double-digit rounds—if you want a guy, go get him. But Sadiq was already regarded as something of a project before he spent much of the offseason sidelined by injury, and the Jets' offense may not offer the same favorable environment Sadiq had at Oregon.

Biggest Surprise: Chris Rodriguez at 10.11

Fantasy managers have spent much of the summer projecting Bhayshul Tuten into a featured role in Jacksonville. However, the Jaguars have praised Rodriguez throughout the summer, and he was available nearly six rounds later in this draft. When choosing between members of a backfield committee, the less expensive option is often the better value.

Best Pick of Round 11: Caleb Williams at 11.08

They say it's better to start a run than to end one, and in the second half of Round 11, a wise manager started one under center with the selection of Caleb Williams. After a solid second season, he is the seventh quarterback off draft boards on average. Here, he was the 11th QB taken.

Best Pick of Round 12: Kaelon Black at 12.06

If you use a first-round pick on Christian McCaffrey, Black is a sensible late-round insurance option. If McCaffrey misses time, Black would likely share work with Jordan James, but he could still offer useful depth and contingent upside.

Best Pick of Round 13: Tre Tucker at 13.02

Someone is going to have to serve as the No. 1 wide receiver for the Raiders this season, and if training camp and the preseason have been any indication, Tucker is that guy. The 5'8", 182-pounder isn't built like a No. 1 wide receiver, but he appears to have developed an early rapport with Kirk Cousins.

Best Pick of Round 14: Malik Willis at 14.03

Miami's offensive outlook has drawn considerable skepticism this offseason. But Willis has quite a bit of rushing upside, and he wouldn't be the first quarterback who became fantasy-relevant largely because of garbage time.

Best Pick of Round 15: Jacksonville Jaguars Defense at 15.09

This is an effective way to draft a defense: target a unit with a favorable Week 1 matchup, such as a home game against Cleveland, select it late and then move on to a new option through waivers when the schedule becomes less favorable.

Best Pick of Round 16: Tyler Loop at 16.12

Kickers are best selected with a final-round pick. The advantage of drafting a high-profile option is typically marginal, so there is little reason to prioritize the position earlier.

Gary Davenport is a two-time Fantasy Sports Writers Association Football Writer of the Year. Follow Gary on X at @IDPGodfather .

articles.title: Biggest Surprises That Could Shake Up the 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: Many of us think we know how the upcoming NFL season will unfold, but every year, we're proved wrong by major shakeups.
articles.body:
Many of us think we know how the upcoming NFL season will unfold, but every year, we're proved wrong by major shakeups.

This year won't be any different. So why not go bold with predictions less than a week before the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers kick off the 2026 campaign?

At this time last year, anyone who said the dynastic Kansas City Chiefs would miss the playoffs, the New England Patriots would appear in the Super Bowl and the Seattle Seahawks, led by quarterback Sam Darnold, would hoist the Lombardi Trophy would have been laughed at.

Let's get into six of the biggest surprises that could change the complexion of the league and how we view certain players—three for the AFC and three for the NFC.

Chargers Miss the Playoffs for First Time in Jim Harbaugh Era

The Los Angeles Chargers are usually the offseason darlings that fail to play up to lofty expectations. Though in fairness, they've made the playoffs with an 11-6 record in back-to-back years under head coach Jim Harbaugh.

This offseason, offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel brings renewed optimism to the Chargers' outlook. He'll work with two-time Pro Bowler Justin Herbert and a talented group of skill-position players at running back, wide receiver and tight end.

While there's tremendous buzz around the Chargers' offense, many have overlooked what the team lost on the defensive side of the ball, particularly on the sideline.

Play-caller Jesse Minter left to become the Ravens' head coach, taking with him the defensive acumen that defined the Chargers over the past two seasons. Under his tutelage, Los Angeles allowed the fewest points in 2024 and ranked ninth in defensive scoring in the previous campaign.

First-time NFL defensive coordinator Chris O'Leary will take over for Minter. Aside from a one-year stint as Western Michigan's defensive coordinator last season, he has been a safeties coach. Sure, every play-caller in the NFL needs a first opportunity, but the Chargers defense could see a significant drop-off from Minter to O'Leary.

Furthermore, the Chargers face a brutal stretch from Weeks 3 through 10: road games against the Buffalo Bills, Seattle Seahawks, Kansas City Chiefs, Los Angeles Rams and Baltimore Ravens, plus home matchups with the Denver Broncos and Houston Texans. They have a Week 7 bye during that span.

Herbert may have a career year in passing, but it may not be enough to get the Chargers to the postseason if their defense gives up points in bunches to playoff-caliber opponents and elite-level quarterbacks.

Cowboys Defense Leaps from Worst to Top-10 Scoring Unit

In 2025, the Dallas Cowboys allowed the most points and the third-most yards. So, of course, they made wholesale changes on defense.

Dallas fired defensive coordinator Matt Eberflus and hired former Philadelphia Eagles defensive backs coach and defensive pass game coordinator Christian Parker to replace him.

Unlike Los Angeles Chargers first-time defensive coordinator Chris O'Leary, Parker has coached in the NFL for several years, dating back to 2019, and he's well-traveled across the league. The 34-year-old held positions with the Green Bay Packers and Denver Broncos before his tenure in Philadelphia.

Parker helped develop cornerback Quinyon Mitchell and versatile defensive back Cooper DeJean, both of whom earned first-team All-Pro honors. The Eagles allowed the fewest passing touchdowns in the NFL last season, and their defense has surrendered the fewest passing yards in the league since the start of the 2024 campaign.

As one of the rising coaches in the league, Parker can turn the Cowboys defense into a stingy unit that ranks within the top 10 in points and yards allowed.

The Cowboys bolstered their pass rush with seasoned veterans, acquiring Rashan Gary from the Packers and signing Von Miller. They also added a couple of rookie first-rounders in defensive back Caleb Downs and edge-rusher Malachi Lawrence. As free-agent pickups, cornerback Cobie Durant and safety Jalen Thompson will fill starting roles.

If linebacker DeMarvion Overshown stays healthy, Dallas' front seven should be stout with Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark on the defensive line and free-agent acquisition Dee Winters alongside him.

NFL fans enjoy poking fun at the Cowboys' lack of recent postseason success, but their defense won't be a laughing matter. Led by Parker, that unit could help lead the team to an NFC East division title.

The Green Bay Packers have concerning roster voids ahead of their season opener against the Minnesota Vikings.

Green Bay placed star edge-rusher Micah Parsons on the physically unable to perform list, which means he'll miss at least the first four games of the season coming off a torn ACL with meniscus damage.

Aside from that, the NFL placed running back Josh Jacobs on the Commissioner's Exempt List after he was charged with battery and criminal damage to property in connection with a May incident involving his girlfriend. His availability for the 2026 season remains uncertain.

Jacobs played a significant role in the Packers' offense, leading a rushing attack that ranked fifth and seventh in total carries over the last two seasons. In his absence, Green Bay will rely on third-year tailback MarShawn Lloyd, who's been beset by injuries, logging just six carries for 15 yards in one career game.

The Packers will start the season without their best defensive player and their most established offensive skill player. They'll open the season with three of their first four games on the road and finish the campaign against the Buffalo Bills, Chicago Bears, Houston Texans and Detroit Lions in four of their last five contests.

Green Bay may stumble through September and October and never recover from a slow start. If the Packers finish last in the NFC North, it would be the first time it's happened since the 2005 season.

Ravens WR Ja'Kobi Lane Makes Quick Rise to Become OROY

Since New Orleans Saints running back Alvin Kamara won 2017 Offensive Rookie of the Year, every player who's won the award was a top-10 pick in his draft class. Ja'Kobi Lane could buck that trend this year.

Lane generated buzz during organized team activities through training camp, and it translated in his preseason debut against the Philadelphia Eagles. In that outing, he caught three passes for 38 yards and a touchdown. Although it's a small in-game sample size, it's all the rookie needed to secure a top roster spot on the depth chart.

Early in the offseason, quarterback Lamar Jackson told reporters that offensive coordinator Declan Doyle's play-calling is "mind-blowing."

During an interview with Adam Schein on SiriusXM, the two-time MVP put defenses across the league on notice.

"I don't believe a defense is prepared for what's in store for them," Jackson said.

If Baltimore's offense is as potent as Jackson says it could be, Lane should be a beneficiary. Wide receiver Rashod Bateman is facing three charges in connection with a June incident, according to Jonas Shaffer of the Baltimore Banner . His status for the season remains uncertain. Even as a No. 2 receiver, Lane could post gaudy numbers as a complement to two-time Pro Bowler Zay Flowers.

At 6'4", 205 pounds, Lane could be a primary red-zone target in addition to his big-play ability outside the 20-yard line. If that's the case, he would have a good chance to follow Kamara's early career path from third-round pick to Offensive Rookie of the Year.

Saints RB Travis Etienne Jr. Emerges as Rushing Champion

After Travis Etienne Jr. sat out his 2021 rookie season with a Lisfranc injury, he's been a solid running back, but his resume isn't filled with accolades—no Pro Bowl or All-Pro campaigns.

On his second team, he could be a breakout candidate in terms of taking a leap from solid to a top-tier running back.

With Alvin Kamara on the mend with an MCL sprain and oft-injured tailback Kendre Miller second on the New Orleans Saints' running back depth chart, Etienne should be in line for a workhorse role early in the season.

Even with Kamara's return, Etienne should continue to handle a bulk of the touches on a new four-year, $48 million contract.

Furthermore, Etienne will run behind an offensive line that features first-rounders Kelvin Banks Jr. and Taliese Fuaga, two-time Pro Bowl center Erik McCoy and free-agent acquisition David Edwards, who helped block for 2025 rushing champion James Cook.

By the way, head coach Kellen Moore called plays for the Philadelphia Eagles when Saquon Barkley threatened Eric Dickerson's single-season rushing record. The Eagles' star tailback racked up a league-leading 2,005 yards before resting in Week 18 of the 2024 season.

Back in his home state, Etienne is set up for a big year with a shot to win the rushing title.

Texans Defense Leads Them to NFL's Best Record at 14-3

The Houston Texans will put defense back in the headlines amid a strong shift to an emphasis on offensive playmakers.

Quarterback C.J. Stroud won 2023 Offensive Rookie of the Year in a Pro Bowl season, but his passing yard and touchdown totals have dipped over the last two years.

Two-time Pro Bowl wideout Nico Collins hasn't played through a full campaign, and he's yet to finish a season with a double-digit touchdown total. Houston acquired 29-year-old running back David Montgomery to lead its ground attack, and he may split a fair number of touches with 2025 fourth-rounder Woody Marks.

The Texans' offense won't be flashy, but their defense could hold teams to historic lows in scoring and yards.

Led by defensive-minded head coach DeMeco Ryans, you would be hard-pressed to find a weakness on his side of the ball. The defense has strengths at all three levels.

First-team All-Pro Will Anderson Jr. and five-time Pro Bowler Danielle Hunter lead a dominant pass rush. Sheldon Rankins and Tommy Togiai are stout run defenders. Behind them, Pro Bowl linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair patrols the middle.

In the secondary, all five of the starting defensive backs in nickel have recorded at least four interceptions in a season over the last two years.

Two-time first-team All-Pro cornerback Derek Stingley Jr., Pro Bowl cornerback Kamari Lassiter, Pro Bowl safety Calen Bullock, slot defender Jalen Pitre and free-agent acquisition Reed Blankenship are all ball hawks.

The Texans' defense should give quarterbacks little time to throw, ball-carriers little room to run and receivers little separation downfield. This is an elite unit that will lead this team deep into the playoffs with the league's best record, proving that a high-level defense can still be a title contender's prime advantage.

Maurice Moton covers the NFL for Bleacher Report. You can follow him on Twitter @MoeMoton .

articles.title: Seydou Traore interview: British tight end on NFL Draft, Miami Dolphins and goals in the league
articles.summary: British tight end Seydou Traore has made the Miami Dolphins' 53-man roster; Dolphins selected Traore with the 180th overall pick (fifth round) in the 2026 NFL Draft; Traore tells Sky Sports about the draft, Miami and how his versatility is his strength
articles.body:
Despite the recent successes of Jay Ajayi, Efe Obada and Jermaine Eluemunor, it is still rare to see a British player in the NFL, and Traore is already on a unique journey

By being selected in the 2026 NFL Draft (fifth round, 180th overall), Traore became the first player to have attended London's NFL Academy and later be drafted to the NFL - after taking part in trials as a 16-year-old at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium all the way back in 2019 .

After moving to Florida to seek a college scholarship, he played two seasons at Arkansas State before transferring to Mississippi State, sitting out a year, then putting together two more seasons that caught the eyes of NFL scouts.

Since being drafted, he has made Miami's initial 53-man roster, but there is a lot more work to do. Traore spoke to Sky Sports this summer about the draft, landing in Miami, and his future in the league...

It was a long road from the NFL Academy to having his name called and walking across the stage in Pittsburgh, and Traore said the draft-day experience was "everything I expected and more".

He said: "Having my mum and my sister there with me meant a lot. Being able to reap the rewards of the years of hard work and the years they haven't been able to see me and be around me. As much as it was for me, it was for them.

"Heading on to that stage is an amazing feeling. I was speechless when I got out there, but yeah, it was amazing."

Unsurprisingly, Traore said he was inundated with "a bunch" of messages from people involved in the International Player Pathway programme, whether players, coaches or staff.

"Everyone from back home was checking up on me, congratulating me and just wishing me the best, saying they've either seen the videos or read this," he said.

"I was more than happy to go through each one and just connect with people and say thank you."

After spending five years in what he called the "countryside" of Arkansas and Mississippi, Traore is back in a lively city.

However, he didn't have much time for exploring. First up was training, conditioning, film, playbook and importantly: forming connections.

The Dolphins are coming off a disappointing 7-10 season, their second straight losing campaign. That meant the end of the Mike McDaniel era and a fresh start in Miami.

For new head coach Jeff Hafley, new general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan, and new quarterback Malik Willis, the main goal is bringing the team together.

"The first thing is connection," Traore explained.

"Connection between the whole team and teammates and everything.

"We'll be eating; no one's on their phones. When they're in this building, people are trying to get better and connect with teammates.

"So at the door, you understand once you get in here, you're coming in with a purpose.

"Everything outside, you can put on pause for a few hours, but get to know the people you're going to be with the whole day. Because those are the people that are going to have your back on the field."

Traore could offer something to a Miami team lacking offensive weapons right now, but it's a long road ahead.

Tight ends rarely make an instant impact, and fifth-round picks face a fight each and every year to make a team.

The 24-year-old understands his situation and knows his career won't be defined by year one.

"It's such a long process," Traore said. "So you've got to look at the far picture."

In his rookie campaign, his plan is "learning, soaking up as much as I can this first year and showing when I do have those chances, showing the ability to make a play."

He has no specific goals or milestones but Traore knows what he can offer to the league, now and in the future.

He said: "I'm versatile. Not just on the field - as a person as well. I adapt pretty well to different stuff.

"I'm a team player. I am willing to do what I need to do for the team's success.

The Miami Dolphins kick off their season by hosting the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, September 13.

The NFL season begins Wednesday, September 10 with a Super Bowl rematch as the Seattle Seahawks host the New England Patriots overnight (1.20am kick-off) live on Sky Sports.

articles.title: “Unbelievable things coming soon": Patrick and Brittany Mahomes take their family brand to the next level with new campaign
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes is adding a distinctly personal touch to his growing off-field profile. With the new NFL season approaching, the Kansas City Chiefs qu.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes is adding a distinctly personal touch to his growing off-field profile. With the new NFL season approaching, the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback has offered fans a first look at a campaign that brings Brittany Mahomes and their three children into the frame. The move highlights how the Mahomes name is becoming more than a football identity, with family, business and entertainment increasingly shaping the quarterback’s public image.Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes bring family into new campaignMahomes shared a short teaser for the upcoming project, titled “Unbelievable,” giving fans a glimpse of himself with Brittany and their children, Sterling, Bronze and Golden.“Unbelievable things coming soon,” Mahomes wrote while sharing the teaser.The message was brief, but the image behind it carried plenty of meaning. Instead of another campaign built around Mahomes alone, the quarterback has chosen to put his entire immediate family at the center of the latest project.That approach fits the way the Mahomes brand has evolved. Patrick remains one of the NFL’s biggest stars, but Brittany has also created a strong public identity of her own through her business interests, sports involvement and social media presence.Their children have also become familiar faces in the family’s public content. The new campaign takes that family visibility a step further by placing all three children alongside their parents in a commercial setting.The timing is also significant. Mahomes is entering his 10th NFL season, a milestone that underlines how much his career and public profile have grown since he became Kansas City’s starting quarterback.Chiefs star Patrick Mahomes expands his off-field brandMahomes has spent years building a profile that stretches well beyond football. His performances with the Chiefs made him a household name, while endorsements and business opportunities have helped turn that sporting success into a broader personal brand.Now, the family appears to be an important part of that story.The “Unbelievable” teaser does not disclose what the full campaign will include, so fans will have to wait for the complete release. Still, the decision to feature Brittany, Sterling, Bronze and Golden suggests the project will lean into the family’s appeal rather than present Mahomes simply as an athlete.That could give the campaign a warmer and more relatable feel. Mahomes is usually seen competing under intense pressure on an NFL field. Here, the focus shifts to the people closest to him.For the Chiefs quarterback, the next chapter is not only about what happens on Sundays. His football career remains the foundation of his fame, but his expanding business interests and family-focused projects show how the Mahomes brand continues to develop away from the stadium.As Kansas City prepares for another season with Mahomes at the helm, the “Unbelievable” campaign offers a glimpse of a different side of the superstar. articles.title: Panthers in same Super Bowl tier as Buccaneers, Falcons, Saints
articles.summary: All four teams in the NFC South, at least according to CBS Sports' Super Bowl tiers, are standing on the same ground at the start of the 2026 season.
articles.body:
The NFC South isn't exactly the cream of the NFL's crop.

In 2025, and for the first time in a decade, the Carolina Panthers won the division . . . at 8-9 . . . and with a -69 point differential. And going into 2026, the outlook for the reigning champs, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , the Atlanta Falcons and the New Orleans Saints doesn't appear too bright.

All four of the NFC South's teams landed in the same Super Bowl tier in CBS Sports' new power rankings by Carter Bahns. Bahns writes:

The C Tier might be the most fluid. If everything clicks for these teams, they can clinch a spot in the playoffs. If it falls apart, they could bottom out and face tough questions about whether to keep their coaching staff and whether to blow up their rosters. Nothing exemplifies that reality quite like the NFC South. All four teams landed in this tier for two reasons. One, they are all on equal footing, as evidenced by the three-way tie atop the division in 2025. Two, none of them are particularly great, which showed in all of them finishing last season under .500.

It's tough to argue that any of these four teams belong in a higher tier.

Atlanta has some of the most talented players in the division, but is also dealing with the worst quarterback situation of the bunch.

Tampa Bay has some great pieces like defensive lineman Vita Vea and second-year receiver Emeka Egbuka. But with quarterback Baker Mayfield and the organization at an impasse over his next contract, their run could soon be coming to an end.

New Orleans could have the most promising quarterback in the division after a very impressive rookie season from Tyler Shough. However, it's going to take a while for them to climb out of the hole they dug for themselves by keeping the Drew Brees-era roster together for far too long after he left.

The Panthers are a wild card based on what they get or don't get from their quarterback, Bryce Young. It's conceivable that they could finish anywhere between 10 wins and five wins, depending on how he does as well as the health of their key pieces.

Bottom line—nobody really knows what to expect from this division.
