articles.title: NFL Execs Rank AFC's Top Teams in Poll Ahead of 2026 Season, Where Do Patriots, Bills, Chiefs Rank?
articles.summary: NFL executives shared mixed opinions on whether Drake Maye will be able to lead the New England Patriots back to another Super Bowl in a new survey published by The Athletic's Mike Sando.
articles.body:
NFL executives shared mixed opinions on whether Drake Maye will be able to lead the New England Patriots back to another Super Bowl in a new survey published by The Athletic's Mike Sando .

The Buffalo Bills performed the best in Sando's survey, with four of six participating NFL executives ranking Josh Allen's squad as the best team in the AFC.

The Denver Broncos (second overall) and Houston Texans (third overall) also received votes as the conference's best team, according to Sando.

49ers DE's Hilarious Plan for Australia Flight

The Patriots averaged fourth place overall but received a wider range of rankings, with one executive ranking the team third in the AFC and another sliding the team all the way down to ninth.

Multiple executives speaking with Sando pointed out the Patriots' favorable schedule last season as a reason to expect Maye and his team to take a step back in 2026.

One executive described the Patriots to Sando as "the No. 1 regression team."

The Baltimore Ravens and Kansas City Chiefs were ranked fifth and sixth overall, respectively, according to Sando. Executives speaking with Sando expressed doubts about the health of both Lamar Jackson and Patrick Mahomes.

The choice for the lowest-ranked club in the AFC was almost unanimous, per Sando. Five out of six executives surveyed by Sando expect the Miami Dolphins to be the worst team in the conference after coach Jeff Hafley told reporters he won't measure success this season by winning.

The Patriots will get the chance to improve their championship odds when opening the season on the road next Wednesday against the defending champion Seattle Seahawks.

C.J. Stroud and the Texans are set to open their own campaign the following Sunday against the visiting Bills, the day before Bo Nix and the Broncos visit the Chiefs in what could be Mahomes' return from knee surgery.

articles.title: Pittsburgh Steelers announce weeklong celebration ahead of season opener against Falcons
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers announced plans Thursday for a weeklong celebration across Pittsburgh leading up to their regular season opener against the Atlanta F...
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers announced plans Thursday for a weeklong celebration across Pittsburgh leading up to their regular season opener against the Atlanta Falcons on Sept. 13 at Acrisure Stadium.

The Steelers Kickoff Week activities will feature community events and interactive displays across six local neighborhoods.

At the center of the celebration is a traveling display featuring giant Super Bowl rings originally created for the 2026 NFL Draft Steelers Country activation.

From Monday through Saturday of game week, the giant Super Bowl rings will visit six different locations across Pittsburgh. At each stop, fans will be invited to participate in a paint-by-numbers project by painting a segment of a larger canvas representing that location.

Once completed, the six individual pieces will be assembled into a single 24-foot mural. The completed artwork will be unveiled to fans at Acrisure Stadium during the team's home opener.

Along the tour route, the Steelers will also host a series of charity and community events in the participating neighborhoods. Steelers Vice President of Strategy Dan Rooney noted that the team designed the activities to maintain connection with local supporters following the city's hosting of the draft.

"What drives the Steelers is our fans," Rooney said. "That's why we're bringing kickoff week excitement directly to them. After welcoming the football world to Pittsburgh for the 2026 NFL Draft, we're taking a piece of that experience into neighborhoods across the city — giving fans a chance to relive the historic event, connect with our team's legacy and build excitement for the season ahead."

Monday, 9/7: Patricia Rooney Memorial Fountain in Allegheny Commons Park, North Side

This location will also kick off a week-long matching campaign benefiting the Salvation Army Harbor Light Center in recognition of the 40th anniversary of Project Bundle-Up, which Patricia Rooney helped to pioneer.

Tuesday, 9/8: U.S. Steel Community Field at Hazelwood Green, Hazelwood

This location will also host a free Steelers Youth Football Mini Camp for youth ages 6-14 from 6:30-8 p.m.

The Oakland stop brings Kickoff Week to the city's college community, just blocks from the former site of Forbes Field, where the Steelers played their first home game in 1933.

Thursday, 9/10: Lawn of Point State Park, Downtown

The rings return to one of Pittsburgh's most iconic locations, Point State Park, where they were first displayed as part of Steelers Country during the 2026 NFL Draft.

Friday, 9/11: Acrisure Stadium, North Shore

To mark the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 terrorist attacks, volunteers will join a nationwide movement to "Honor Through Action." As part of the largest annual day of service in U.S. history, volunteers will pack more than 248,500 healthy, non-perishable meals for local families at risk of hunger. All meals packed will be donated to the Greater Pittsburgh Community Food Bank for distribution to local individuals and families in need.

Saturday, 9/12: Duquesne Incline Overlook, Mt. Washington

The Steelers will cover Duquesne Incline fares from 12-2 p.m.

Sunday, 9/13: Kickoff Game, Steelers vs. Falcons at Acrisure Stadium

All six Super Bowl rings and the completed fan-painted mural will arrive at Acrisure Stadium as the week-long journey culminates on gameday.
